# Copilot instructions — DFMEA Workshop Studio

## What this repository is
DFMEA Workshop Studio is a single-page web app that guides a cross-functional design team through a Design Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (DFMEA) workshop at a health-technology company. It follows the AIAG-VDA 7-step method with 1–10 severity, occurrence and detection scales, and links failure effects to ISO 14971 hazards. An AI facilitator panel calls Microsoft 365 Copilot to suggest failure modes and actions, ask facilitation questions, challenge ratings and summarize the workshop. Voice dictation and read-aloud are built in.

The app was generated with App Builder in Microsoft 365 Copilot and runs as a Managed Runtime app (identity and connector references in `ms.config.json`). Supported release paths include App Builder and the Managed Runtime `ms` CLI with platform-managed Git/build. See `docs/HANDOVER.md` for the separate CAPE target, current migration blockers and release procedure. Never reuse the source app identity for the CAPE migration.

## Stack
- React 19 + TypeScript (strict) + Vite 7, Tailwind CSS 4 (design tokens in `src/index.css`), shadcn/ui on Radix (`src/components/ui/*`).
- TanStack Query 5 for every async/connector call, zustand 5 for shared state if needed, react-router-dom 7 (`src/routes.tsx`), lucide-react, sonner, date-fns.
- `@microsoft/managed-apps` 0.5.11 — the connector runtime behind the generated client in `generated/`.
- All packages resolve from the public npm registry. Use Node.js 22 LTS (Vite 7 needs Node 20.19+ or 22.12+).

## Build and validate — run all three before every commit and pull request
```bash
npm ci                 # install from package-lock.json
npm run typecheck      # tsc -p tsconfig.app.json --noEmit
npm run lint           # eslint . — 0 errors expected; 2 fast-refresh warnings in template files are known
npm run build:check    # production build without writing files
```
- `npm run build` writes `dist/`; `npm run dev` serves on http://localhost:5173.
- `build:check` uses POSIX environment syntax: on Windows run it in Git Bash or WSL (CI runs on Linux).
- `npm run check` runs the three checks in parallel but needs bun (`bun run check`).
- Voice regression tests use the Node built-in runner and existing dependencies: `node --test tests/*.test.mjs`. Adding a test dependency still needs approval.
- Deployment tooling is isolated from app dependencies: pinned `@microsoft/managed-apps-cli@0.32.2` requires Node 24.11+, while this app remains on Node 22 and its frozen SDK.

## Data model (`src/data/dfmea.ts`)
`DfmeaProject` → `StructureElement` (tree via `parentId`; System, Subsystem, Component) → `DesignFunction` (with `requirementRef`).
`StructureElement` → `FailureMode` (`functionId`, `effect`, `severity`, `hazardRef`) → `FailureCause` (`occurrence`, `detection`, prevention and detection controls, `priority`) → `ImprovementAction` (`kind`, `owner`, `due`, `status`).
- Severity belongs to the failure mode's effect; occurrence and detection belong to each cause. RPN = S × O × D, shown only when all three are rated.
- Action priority is chosen by the team; it is not computed.
- `origin` (`team` | `ai`) and `reviewed` mark AI-suggested content until the team confirms it.
- State is in-memory React state seeded from `SAMPLE_DFMEA` (a fictional product). Nothing persists across reloads yet.

## AI facilitator contract
- Only `src/connectors/workiq-copilot-chat.ts` talks to Copilot, through the generated `WorkIQCopilotMCPService.mcp_m365copilot` (Work IQ Copilot MCP connector, in preview). It sends a JSON-RPC 2.0 `tools/call` for the tool `copilot_chat` with one argument, `message`: no `initialize` or `tools/list` handshake, no session id, a unique id per request.
- Reply path: `result.content[]` text blocks → JSON envelope (`reply`, or `rawResponse.messages[]`) → assistant text. Echoes of the prompt are rejected.
- `callWorkIqCopilotChatItems(prompt, flatSchema)` returns validated rows; it is used for failure-mode and action suggestions that can be added to the DFMEA. `callWorkIqCopilotChatText(prompt)` returns answer text for questions, rating challenges, summaries and free questions.
- Errors are typed — `WorkIqConnectorError` (HTTP status), `WorkIqToolError`, `WorkIqResponseError` (`stage`) — and mapped to user-safe messages with a short code. Never show raw upstream error text, and never turn a failure into an empty result.
- Copilot calls take about 30 seconds: keep them single-flight with `retry: false`, show progress and keep prompts short.
- Copilot output is untrusted text: render it as text (never `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`), validate it before it enters the model, and store it with `origin: "ai"` and `reviewed: false`.
- Connector calls only work inside the managed-app host (the published app or the App Builder preview). Under `npm run dev` on localhost there is no host, so calls fail after a ~30-second handshake timeout; the rest of the app works locally.
- Work IQ connector requests have a hard 30-second host timeout. Keep calls single-flight, report that limit accurately, and do not imply the app can increase it.
- Realtime voice is a speech layer, not a second source of answers: configure the voice model to call `ask_copilot` for every user question and return the selected helper's result. Work IQ remains default; three published FRE specialists use generated `DFMEASpecialistMCPService` operations, never browser-direct Power Platform requests. Manual selection applies to typed and voice with no fallback. The browser connects by WebRTC directly to Azure OpenAI using the broker's ephemeral credential. Never put keys or secrets in app source, browser storage or logs.
- Helper switching/new conversation ends voice/read-aloud, resets output/initialization/conversation ID, and invalidates late replies between handshake stages and after tool execution. Keep IDs/selection in session memory only. Only Work IQ exposes the app's file-search toggle. Validate bounded SSE, unique matching JSON-RPC result IDs, MCP errors, response envelope and GUID continuity. HTTP-200 environment-policy rejections are failures, not clarification. The MCP specialist's 180-second app-side wait covers handshake plus answer but cannot extend connector/server timeouts or cancel an upstream connector; retain single-flight until settlement. Work IQ's host limit and the separate voice-setup deadline remain 30 seconds.
- The specialists use the GitHub Copilot harness: never restore `ExecuteCopilotAsyncV2`, which explicitly rejects it. User-published agents expose supported MCP channels in `Managed_App_Deploy_FRE` (`75660de8-d408-e9ce-bc60-84d4f6a30d0b`), with schemas `_20cdd7`, `_5a9a6a` and `_7867b1`. The narrow generated connector remains in the app environment, using dedicated single-tenant client `c728a6e3-0558-432d-aafa-74324ed47c5e` and only delegated `MCS.InvokeAsMCP`. User acceptance confirms all three hosted typed answers and selected-specialist live text/audio/microphone release at release `7520e85d4c4ae27539f5611c611e03a4817493de`. Do not claim independent instrumented traces. No app move, agent/model edit, governance weakening or browser Power Platform fetch.
- The realtime voice button is shown only when `AiFacilitator` receives a generated `requestRealtimeToken` callback. Add the broker through App Builder or supported `ms app add data-source` / `refresh data-source` tooling and use its generated client; never hand-write generated connector clients. The exact Azure OpenAI origin also needs a Managed Runtime CSP `connect-src` allowlist entry.
- The app stays in `Managed_App_Deploy` (`28207d24-1fb8-e2ed-ba6e-180550d63611`). App `088be080-35da-497a-a83e-0b870c975893` is live at https://play.managedapps.cloud.microsoft/apps/088be080-35da-497a-a83e-0b870c975893 at release `7520e85d4c4ae27539f5611c611e03a4817493de`; prior voice-only rollback is `12c6ed88787190bceb77602cde62d5908262f4d0`. Only specialists live in FRE. The handover is the release-evidence source; do not infer deployment from source commits/codegen. Rotate the connector's commissioning credential before its recorded expiry, never by committing secrets or creating broader/long-lived access.
- The user approved Managed Environment protection (`Basic` to `Standard`) and dedicated group `Managed_App_Deploy_CSP` (`a4af58d4-d70a-411f-a8e1-43af08ab72fd`). CSP-only policy `0ea9b73c-d80e-4ecf-a8a0-0a74450be1ab` adds only `https://dfmea-voice-fy27.openai.azure.com` to `Connect-Src`, with enforcement enabled. Assignment, membership and materialized environment settings were verified; the user subsequently reported working live voice. That report is not an agent-observed full audio/Stop trace. Do not weaken governance, add ACP/DLP rules, duplicate policies or claim voice E2E success from token issuance/build/preflight.
- Opening the voice console must not acquire the microphone; Start is explicit. Stop must work during setup, and every dialog dismissal stops the session. Show activity only from real session/tool/audio events, never fake transcripts or level meters. Preserve reduced-motion and forced-colors support.
- Reuse protected CLI authentication and the target repository's Keychain-backed Git helper; do not repeatedly initiate sign-in, persist tokens in plaintext or create long-lived credentials. Native Git and the CLI use separate auth clients. Ignore `.ms/` caches containing signed schema-icon URLs rather than bypassing native secret scanning.

## Rules
- Never edit `generated/**`, `ms.config.json` (except `description`), `vite.config.ts`, `vite-dev-reload.ts`, `tsconfig*.json`, `eslint.config.js`, `components.json`, `index.html`, `src/App.tsx`, `src/main.tsx`, `src/components/ui/**`, or any file marked LOCKED in `AGENTS.md`.
- Treat `package.json`, `package-lock.json` and `bun.lock` as frozen unless a change is explicitly approved; if one is approved, update both lockfiles.
- Keep `export function HomePage()` in `src/pages/home.tsx`. Add a page as a named-export file plus one entry in `src/routes.tsx`.
- New connectors and data sources are generated by App Builder or supported Managed Runtime CLI commands. Only those tools may write `generated/` and app identity/bindings in `ms.config.json`. App code must never hand-write connector clients or call Graph or Power Platform APIs directly.
- Accessibility is required: one `<main>` (owned by the shell), full keyboard operation, visible focus, `aria-pressed`/`aria-expanded`/`aria-current`/`aria-selected` for state, color never the only cue, forced-colors support, and text contrast of at least 4.5:1 in light and dark mode.
- Use semantic color tokens (`bg-background`, `bg-card`, `text-muted-foreground`, …). Status and priority colors only come from the tone map in `dfmea-ui.tsx`. Keep workflow status and urgency as separate fields.
- Use `useConfirm()` instead of `window.confirm`/`alert`, register shortcuts only through `useAppShortcut`, never add raw `keydown` listeners, and wrap any `localStorage` access in try/catch.
- No sample, demo or test-data labels, fake sign-in widgets or data-source badges in the UI.
- Don't invent DFMEA thresholds, classifications or rating tables. For example, the AIAG-VDA action-priority table must come from the licensed handbook supplied by the team.
- Keep `docs/HANDOVER.md` current when status, backlog or release steps change.
